subject.title: [Bug]: non_deliverable_terminal_turn produces no outbound notification to channel plugins — Octo (and other channels) go silent

question: Should OpenClaw surface `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` to channel plugins by automatically pushing a core fallback through normal outbound delivery, by adding a public plugin SDK terminal-failure hook, or by leaving this responsibility to individual channel plugins?
rationale: Both viable fixes change user-visible delivery semantics and at least one option changes the plugin SDK contract, so automation should not choose the permanent owner boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Core automatic fallback
options.body: Core synthesizes and delivers the fallback text through the existing outbound path so current and future channel plugins get a visible failure by default.

options.title: Plugin SDK terminal hook
options.body: OpenClaw adds a documented terminal-failure callback that gives plugins control but requires each channel plugin to implement the new API.

options.title: Plugin-owned workaround only
options.body: OpenClaw leaves the core contract unchanged and expects Octo and other plugins to inspect run state or repair their own delivery loops.

recommendation.title: Core automatic fallback
recommendation.body: Core synthesizes and delivers the fallback text through the existing outbound path so current and future channel plugins get a visible failure by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this area to silent-turn fail-closed behavior and plugin SDK outbound reply routing.
